title: To lower the age at which a minor may be tried as an adult for certain criminal offenses in the District of Columbia to 14 years of age.
official_title: To lower the age at which a minor may be tried as an adult for certain criminal offenses in the District of Columbia to 14 years of age.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Brandon Gill (R-TX) with 6 cosponsors. The House-passed measure has moved to the Senate per the latest recorded action.
summary: Amends two sections of the District of Columbia Official Code to lower the age at which a minor may be treated as an adult in criminal proceedings for certain offenses. In section 16-2301(3) the exclusion threshold moves from "sixteen years of age" to "fourteen years of age." In section 16-2307(a) the ages at which a minor may be transferred to a criminal proceeding drop from "fifteen," "sixteen," and "eighteen" to "fourteen" in paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) respectively. The changes apply to criminal offenses committed on and after the date of enactment.
brief: Amends the D.C. Official Code to lower the age at which a minor may be excluded from Family Court jurisdiction, or transferred to a criminal proceeding, from sixteen/fifteen/eighteen to fourteen — applying to offenses committed on or after enactment.

sections.label: Section 1 — Lowering Age at Which a Minor May Be Tried as Adult for Certain Criminal Offenses in District of Columbia

items.main: Subsection (a) amends section 16-2301, D.C. Official Code, paragraph (3), by striking "sixteen years of age" and inserting "fourteen years of age," and by striking "the age of sixteen" and inserting "the age of fourteen" in the matter following subparagraph (C).
items.detail: The bill leaves the surrounding structure of paragraph (3) intact; only the two age references are changed.

items.main: Subsection (b) amends section 16-2307(a), D.C. Official Code, striking "fifteen" in paragraph (1) and inserting "fourteen," striking "sixteen" in paragraph (2) and inserting "fourteen," and striking "eighteen" in paragraph (3) and inserting "fourteen."
items.detail: All three paragraph-level age thresholds for transfer to a criminal proceeding are moved to the same fourteen-year figure.

items.main: Subsection (c) applies the Act and its amendments only to criminal offenses committed on and after the date of enactment.
items.detail: Offenses committed before enactment remain governed by the pre-amendment ages.

gaps: The bill does not restate which categories of offenses trigger the exclusion or transfer, since those criteria are set in the surrounding text of sections 16-2301 and 16-2307 rather than in this Act.
The bill does not modify the procedural safeguards that accompany a transfer determination in section 16-2307.
The bill does not address parallel age references elsewhere in the D.C. Official Code that govern juvenile custody, records, or sentencing.
The bill does not include an appropriation or resource plan for the D.C. courts or corrections agencies that would handle the change.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Comer
featured_quotes.text: We have debated these bills in a sincere effort to work with the President of the United States to lower crime in D.C. We have heard nothing from the Democrats other than there is no crime problem in D.C., and that a solution is to make Washington, D.C., a State. We are serious about lowering crime. We applaud the efforts of the President of the United States. We will continue to work with him to make our Capital City as safe as possible. I appreciate Brandon Gill, the sponsor of the bill, and Byron Donalds for sponsoring the last bill.

featured_quotes.name: Ms. Pressley
featured_quotes.text: This bill seeks to create 14-year-old prisoners in the adult criminal legal system. We know this approach doesn't improve public safety. It only traumatizes our babies. History tells us as much. Antron McCray, 15 years old; Yusef Salaam, 15 years old; Raymond Santana, 14 years old; Korey Wise, 16 years old; and Kevin Richardson, 14 years old. These five boys with big smiles and bright futures ahead of them went on to experience fear and manipulation that no child should.
